source_refs: Heidegger GA7 Die Frage nach der Technik pp.7–8,20–22

from_node.description: Modern technologies are human-made means to ends and can be described instrumentally.

to_node.description: Therefore the instrumental-anthropological definition exhausts what Heidegger is trying to diagnose as the essence of modern technology.

bridge.statement: Heidegger calls the instrumental definition correct but insufficient and names Gestell as a way of revealing/order rather than a technical object.

ge4.alternative_disclosure: poietic bringing-forth and other modes of revealing remain conceptually distinct
ge4.discriminator: show a distinctive ordering/revealing structure beyond generic means-end use
ge4.revision_trigger: cases where the Gestell vocabulary merely redescribes ordinary instrumentality without additional explanatory discrimination
